children: Airbus

expects the global market for commercial aviation services to more than double to $420 billion by 2045, driven by an expanding aircraft fleet, rising passenger traffic and growing demand for maintenance, digital technology and workforce training.

The European aircraft manufacturer forecasts that the services market will grow at a compound annual rate of 3.8% from 2026 through 2045, according to its latest global services forecast. The worldwide commercial aircraft fleet is projected to reach 45,550 planes by 2045, while annual passenger traffic is expected to double to 10 billion travelers.
Fleet expansions

For investors, the forecast highlights revenue opportunities extending beyond new aircraft deliveries to include maintenance, replacement parts, engineering support and technology upgrades. An expanding and aging fleet could provide recurring business for Airbus and other aerospace suppliers, while increasing demand for maintenance capacity and skilled labor could create operational constraints and additional costs for airlines.
Aircraft maintenance spending

Off-wing maintenance, which includes engine and component servicing, is projected to reach $217 billion by 2045, growing at an annual rate of 3.7%. Airbus expects demand to increase as aircraft age and require more frequent shop visits, supporting spending on replacement parts and repairs.

Maintenance operations support, a newly defined category covering inventory management and engineering services, is forecast to reach $104 billion, growing 4.3% annually. On-wing maintenance, including routine inspections and heavier aircraft checks, is expected to grow 2.8% annually to $36 billion.
Digital services growth
Digital technology and connectivity represent the fastest-growing segment, with Airbus

projecting a 5.3% annual growth rate and a market value of $27 billion by 2045, roughly triple its current size. Airlines are expected to invest in predictive maintenance, real-time aircraft monitoring and connected systems to reduce disruptions and improve operational efficiency.
Meanwhile, aircraft modifications and upgrades, including cabin refurbishments and technology installations, are forecast to reach $21 billion, growing 2.6% annually.
Growing labor requirements

The expansion will require more than 2.44 million additional aviation workers over the next two decades, including 730,000 maintenance technicians, 660,000 pilots and 1.05 million cabin crew members, Airbus

estimates. The company projects that the aviation training services market will reach $17 billion by 2045, growing at a compound annual rate of 3.1%. The anticipated hiring requirements underscore the importance of training capacity as airlines expand operations.
Asia to lead regional growth

Europe and the Commonwealth of Independent States, North America and China are expected to remain the largest aviation services markets by total demand. However, Airbus forecasts that Asia, including Asia-Pacific, China and South Asia, will experience the fastest growth. The projections cover passenger aircraft with more than 100 seats and freighters capable of carrying payloads exceeding 10 metric tons, regardless of manufacturer.
Airbus seeks bigger role

Cristina Aguilar Grieder, senior vice president of customer services for commercial aircraft at Airbus, said the company is expanding its services operations to address the needs of a growing fleet throughout the aircraft lifecycle. Its strategy includes predictive maintenance, fleet modernization and digital systems designed to improve aircraft availability and reliability. The forecast points to a potentially expanding aftermarket business for aerospace manufacturers and suppliers, although the projected industrywide spending doesn't indicate how much revenue Airbus itself expects to capture.

title: Airbus sees aviation services doubling to $420B by 2045
